meta.titre: Vertebrate Classes: sorting fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals by their features
meta.sous_theme: Features of the five classes of vertebrates

sections.contenu_markdown: At a market near a river, you can find a tilapia on a stall, frogs in a basket, a live hen, a goat being sold and a snake skin hanging for sale. All of them have a backbone, yet they belong to five different classes. GCE questions give you a feature such as live birth or moist skin and ask which class it matches. To answer correctly you need a short list of the features that separate the classes.

items: Vertebrates are animals with a backbone, and invertebrates have none.
Gaseous exchange takes place at gills, lungs or the skin.
Fertilisation is the fusion of a male gamete and a female gamete.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Two useful words
A **poikilothermic** animal (cold-blooded) has a body temperature that changes with the temperature of its surroundings. A **homoiothermic** (also spelt homeothermic) animal, or warm-blooded animal, keeps its body temperature almost constant.

### The classes compared

| Class | Body covering | Breathing | Reproduction | Body temperature | Other features |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fish | Wet scales (bony fish) | Gills | Many soft eggs laid in water, usually fertilised outside the body | Poikilothermic | Fins, streamlined body |
| Amphibians | Moist, smooth skin without scales | Gills in the larva; lungs and moist skin in the adult | Jelly-coated eggs laid in water, usually fertilised outside the body | Poikilothermic | Larva changes into adult (metamorphosis) |
| Reptiles | Dry, waterproof scales | Lungs | Internal fertilisation; most lay leathery-shelled eggs on land | Poikilothermic | Most live on land |
| Birds | Feathers (scales on the legs) | Lungs | Internal fertilisation; hard-shelled eggs | Homoiothermic | Wings, beak without teeth |
| Mammals | Hair or fur | Lungs, with a diaphragm | Internal fertilisation; most give birth to live young | Homoiothermic | Mammary glands that make milk, sweat glands, teeth of different kinds |

### Viviparous and oviparous
An **oviparous** animal lays eggs. A **viviparous** animal gives birth to live young that developed inside the mother. Most mammals are viviparous.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a description is given and you must name the class
variantes.contenu_markdown: Look for a feature that belongs to one class only: feathers means bird; hair and mammary glands mean mammal; moist scaleless skin and a larval stage with gills mean amphibian; dry scales and lungs with shelled eggs on land mean reptile; gills and fins with wet scales mean fish. Living place and shape do not decide the class.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When readings are taken at different surrounding temperatures
variantes.contenu_markdown: If the animal's temperature rises and falls with the surroundings it is poikilothermic, so it is a fish, an amphibian or a reptile. If it stays almost constant it is homoiothermic, so it is a bird or a mammal.

variantes.nom: Animals that look like another class
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the animal lives in a surprising habitat or moves in a surprising way
variantes.contenu_markdown: A whale or a dolphin lives in water but has lungs, hair, and feeds its young with milk, so it is a mammal. A bat flies but has hair and mammary glands, so it is a mammal. A sea turtle lives in the sea but has dry scales and lungs, so it is a reptile.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Three animals are described.

Animal P: dry scales cover its body; it breathes with lungs; it lays leathery-shelled eggs in a hole on land; its body temperature changes with the air.

Animal Q: its body is covered with hair; the young are born alive and are fed on milk; it has external ears.

Animal R: its skin is smooth and moist; it lays jelly-coated eggs in a pond; the young breathe with gills and the adult uses lungs and skin.

Name the class of each animal and give two reasons for each.

etapes.action: Underline the decisive feature in each description.
etapes.justification: One strong feature is enough to name a class, and a second feature gives the extra mark.
etapes.resultat_markdown: P: dry scales and shelled eggs on land. Q: hair and milk. R: moist skin and gills in the young.

etapes.action: Match animal P to a class.
etapes.justification: Dry waterproof scales, lungs and leathery eggs laid on land are typical of reptiles.

etapes.action: Match animal Q to a class.
etapes.justification: Hair and mammary glands belong only to mammals; live birth supports this.

etapes.action: Match animal R to a class.
etapes.justification: Moist scaleless skin, eggs in water and a larva with gills point to amphibians.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **P is a reptile** (dry scales; leathery-shelled eggs on land; poikilothermic). **Q is a mammal** (hair; young fed on milk; external ears). **R is an amphibian** (moist skin; jelly-coated eggs laid in water; larva with gills, adult with lungs and skin).

items.erreur_markdown: Reptiles have moist skin like amphibians.
items.pourquoi_faux: Reptile skin is dry and covered with scales that prevent water loss. Moist skin is typical of amphibians.
items.correction_markdown: Reptiles: dry scaly skin. Amphibians: moist, smooth skin.

items.erreur_markdown: A dolphin is a fish because it lives in water.
items.pourquoi_faux: The habitat does not decide the class. A dolphin has lungs, is homoiothermic and feeds its young with milk.

items.erreur_markdown: Cold-blooded means that the blood of the animal is always cold.
items.pourquoi_faux: A poikilothermic animal has a body temperature that changes with the surroundings, so it can be warm on a hot day.
items.correction_markdown: Cold-blooded (poikilothermic) means that body temperature varies with the surroundings.

items.erreur_markdown: Every animal that lays eggs is a bird.
items.pourquoi_faux: Fish, amphibians and reptiles also lay eggs. Only birds have feathers.
items.correction_markdown: Use feathers to identify a bird, not egg laying.

items.erreur_markdown: An adult frog breathes with gills.
items.pourquoi_faux: The tadpole breathes with gills, but the adult uses lungs and its moist skin.
items.correction_markdown: Larva: gills. Adult amphibian: lungs and moist skin.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the class of vertebrate to which each animal belongs and give one feature: (a) tilapia, (b) toad, (c) python, (d) hen, (e) goat.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Tilapia: **fish**; has gills and fins.
(b) Toad: **amphibian**; moist skin and a tadpole stage.
(c) Python: **reptile**; dry scales.
(d) Hen: **bird**; has feathers.
(e) Goat: **mammal**; has hair and mammary glands.

items.enonce_markdown:
The body temperature of two animals was measured when the air temperature was changed.

| Air temperature (degrees C) | Animal A body temperature | Animal B body temperature |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 11 | 40 |
| 20 | 21 | 40 |
| 30 | 31 | 40 |

(a) Which animal is poikilothermic? Give a reason from the data.
(b) By how many degrees did the body temperature of A change when the air changed from 10 to 30 degrees C?
(c) Name the classes to which A and B could belong.
(d) State one way in which B keeps its body temperature constant in cold air.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Animal A**: its body temperature follows the air temperature, while that of B stays at 40.
(b) 31 - 11 = **20 degrees C**.
(c) A: **fish, amphibian or reptile** (poikilothermic). B: **bird or mammal** (homoiothermic).
(d) Any one of: heat from respiration in the body; an insulating covering of feathers or hair; shivering.

items.enonce_markdown:
Explain the class of each animal and say why the habitat or the way of moving could mislead a learner.

(a) A bat flies at night.
(b) A sea turtle spends most of its life in the sea.
(c) A tadpole lives in water but the adult frog lives mainly on land.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) A bat is a **mammal**: it has hair and mammary glands and is homoiothermic. Flying makes some learners think of birds, but it has no feathers.
(b) A sea turtle is a **reptile**: it has dry scales, breathes with lungs and lays shelled eggs on land. Living in the sea makes some learners think of fish.
(c) Both are the same **amphibian** at different stages of life. The tadpole has gills for use in water. The adult has lungs and moist skin so it can live on land, but it still needs water or damp places for breeding.

items_markdown: The five classes are fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
Fish, amphibians and reptiles are poikilothermic; birds and mammals are homoiothermic.
Feathers identify birds; hair and mammary glands identify mammals; dry scales and lungs identify reptiles; moist scaleless skin identifies amphibians; gills and fins identify fish.
Most mammals are viviparous, but egg laying alone does not identify a class.
The habitat or the way of moving does not decide the class: dolphins and bats are mammals.
